subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this internal yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix once the conflicted head is refreshed and benchmarked against current main?
rationale: The implementation is plausible and focused, but bootstrap context is a compatibility-sensitive prompt/session surface and the custom glob semantics plus scheduling changes require an owner to accept the upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Refresh, Benchmark, Then Land
options.body: Resolve conflicts and require a current-main versus current-head elapsed-time, liveness, match-parity, and RSS comparison before merging the focused fix.

options.title: Accept Existing Proof
options.body: Resolve conflicts and merge after exact-head checks while accepting that the existing proof exercises the real PR path but not a current-main baseline.

options.title: Pause For Broader Design
options.body: Hold or close the branch if owners prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching instead of maintaining a custom bootstrap glob walker.

recommendation.title: Refresh, Benchmark, Then Land
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts and require a current-main versus current-head elapsed-time, liveness, match-parity, and RSS comparison before merging the focused fix.
